| `server.cors.allowed_origins` | list | empty | Origins as `scheme://host[:port]` | Browser origins besides the server's own that may read `/api`. Empty sends no CORS headers. |
| `server.auth.session_lifetime` | duration | `168h` | A duration | The longest a sign-in lasts, whatever the activity. |
| `server.auth.idle_timeout` | duration | `24h` | A duration | How long a session survives with no requests. |
| `server.auth.cookie_secure` | bool | `true` | `true`, `false` | Sends the session cookie over HTTPS only. Set `false` to sign in over plain HTTP from anywhere but `localhost`. |
| `server.mcp.enabled` | bool | `false` | `true`, `false` | Serves the [MCP endpoint](<https://pushkar-anand.github.io/jocasta/0.15/integrations/mcp/index.md>) at `/mcp`. While off, `/mcp` answers 404. |

## db

| Key | Type | Default | Allowed values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `db.path` | string | `.` | A directory | Where the SQLite file lives. The container image sets `/data`. |
| `db.name` | string | `jocasta.db` | A file name | The SQLite file's name. |

## logger

| Key | Type | Default | Allowed values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `logger.level` | string | `info` | `debug`, `info`, `warn`, `error` | The lowest level logged. Any other value logs at `info`. |
| `logger.format` | string | `json` | `json`, `text` | How each log line is written. Any value but `text` writes JSON. |

## inventory

| Key | Type | Default | Allowed values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `inventory.online_window` | duration | `15m` | A duration | How long after its last sighting a device counts as online. Past it, a [watched device](<https://pushkar-anand.github.io/jocasta/0.15/notifications/watch/index.md>) goes quiet. |
| `inventory.address_grace` | duration | `6h` | A duration | How long an address can go unseen before a later sweep that finds the device elsewhere retires it. Raise it on a network with long DHCP leases. |

## retention

Once an hour, Jocasta deletes the records that are older than their window. `0s` keeps that kind of record forever.

| Key | Type | Default | Allowed values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `retention.history` | duration | `2160h` (90 days) | A duration; `0s` keeps forever | How long Jocasta keeps the change log and the scan log. |
| `retention.traffic` | duration | `720h` (30 days) | A duration; `0s` keeps forever | How long Jocasta keeps the hourly traffic totals. |
| `retention.dns` | duration | `720h` (30 days) | A duration; `0s` keeps forever | How long Jocasta keeps the hourly lookup counts, and the addresses in the answers to lookups. |
| `retention.devices` | duration | `2160h` (90 days) | A duration; `0s` keeps forever | How long Jocasta keeps a device after a scan last saw it. Jocasta keeps a device that you labelled, grouped, typed, noted, ignored or watched. |

## location

| Key | Type | Default | Allowed values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `location.country` | string | empty | A two-letter country code, such as `AU` | The country from which the world map draws its lines. If empty, Jocasta uses the outside address of the router. This address cannot find the country of a network behind carrier-grade NAT. See [NetFlow](<https://pushkar-anand.github.io/jocasta/0.15/plugins/netflow/index.md>). |
| `location.timezone` | string | empty | An IANA zone name, such as `Australia/Sydney` | The zone in which Jocasta shows times. If empty, Jocasta uses `TZ` or the zone of the system, which is UTC in a container. Jocasta always stores times in UTC. |

## networks

| Key | Type | Default | Allowed values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `networks` | list | the host's network | Prefixes, such as `192.0.2.0/24` | The prefixes that the sweep covers at each interval. Jocasta records each address that it finds under the network that contains it. If the list is empty, Jocasta sweeps the network of the host's default route. It does this only if the network is a `/22` or smaller. |

## scan

| Key | Type | Default | Allowed values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `scan.source` | string | `sweep:<hostname>` | Any name | The source name of the sweeps that run at each interval. Set it in a container, where the host name changes on every run. A new name starts a new source. Past scans stay under the old name. |
| `scan.devices.enabled` | bool | `true` | `true`, `false` | Sweeps `networks` on a timer. |
| `scan.devices.interval` | duration | `5m` | A duration | How often the sweep runs. |
| `scan.devices.rate` | int | `1000` | A whole number | The most ICMP probes sent per second. |
| `scan.devices.rounds` | int | `2` | A whole number | The number of probes to each address before Jocasta counts the address as down. |
| `scan.devices.wait` | duration | `2s` | A duration | How long to wait for replies after the last probe. |
| `scan.devices.resolve_names` | bool | `true` | `true`, `false` | Looks up reverse DNS for each address that answered. See [Name devices](<https://pushkar-anand.github.io/jocasta/0.15/naming/index.md>). |
| `scan.devices.resolve_macs` | bool | `true` | `true`, `false` | Reads the neighbour table for hardware addresses. |
| `scan.devices.resolve_mdns` | bool | `true` | `true`, `false` | Asks each device without a reverse DNS name for its name over mDNS. |
| `scan.devices.resolve_netbios` | bool | `true` | `true`, `false` | Asks each device still without a name over NetBIOS. |
| `scan.devices.resolve_dnssd` | bool | `true` | `true`, `false` | Asks for the services that devices advertise. Names each device that still has no name after the name that it gives its services. Needs host networking. |
| `scan.devices.resolve_ssdp` | bool | `true` | `true`, `false` | Searches over SSDP. Names each device that still has no name after its UPnP `friendlyName`. Needs host networking. |
| `scan.ports.enabled` | bool | `false` | `true`, `false` | Probes every known address for open TCP ports on a timer. |
| `scan.ports.interval` | duration | `6h` | A duration | How often the port scan runs. |
| `scan.ports.custom` | string | empty | Ports and ranges, such as `22,80,443,8000-8100`; `1-65535` for every port | The ports to probe. If empty, Jocasta uses a preset. Jocasta also probes each address on the ports that its device advertises. |
| `scan.ports.concurrency` | int | `64` | A whole number | The most connections a scan opens at once. Lower it on a router with a small connection table. |

## plugins

By default, plugins are off. Each instance is under its kind, with a name that you choose as its key. An instance is off, unless it has `enabled: true`. See [Plugins](<https://pushkar-anand.github.io/jocasta/0.15/plugins/index.md>).

### plugins.routeros

A [MikroTik RouterOS](<https://pushkar-anand.github.io/jocasta/0.15/plugins/routeros/index.md>) router, switch or access point.

| Key | Type | Default | Allowed values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `plugins.routeros.<instance>.enabled` | bool | `false` | `true`, `false` | Reads this source. |
| `plugins.routeros.<instance>.host` | string | none, required | An address or host name, without a port | Where the REST API is. |
| `plugins.routeros.<instance>.port` | int | `80`, or `443` with `ssl` | 1 to 65535 | The REST API's port. |
| `plugins.routeros.<instance>.user` | string | empty | A RouterOS user | A read-only user is enough. |
| `plugins.routeros.<instance>.password` | string | empty | Any | The user's password. |
| `plugins.routeros.<instance>.ssl` | bool | `false` | `true`, `false` | Uses HTTPS. Without it, the password goes over the network as plain text, and Jocasta logs a warning. |
| `plugins.routeros.<instance>.insecure` | bool | `false` | `true`, `false` | Skips certificate checks, for RouterOS's self-signed certificate. |
| `plugins.routeros.<instance>.timeout` | duration | `10s` | A duration | The longest one read may take. |
| `plugins.routeros.<instance>.topology_only` | bool | `false` | `true`, `false` | Reads only what is connected to this switch or access point. The router lists its devices. See [Show what is plugged in where](<https://pushkar-anand.github.io/jocasta/0.15/plugins/topology/index.md>). |

### plugins.openwrt

An [OpenWrt](<https://pushkar-anand.github.io/jocasta/0.15/plugins/openwrt/index.md>) router or access point.

| Key | Type | Default | Allowed values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `plugins.openwrt.<instance>.enabled` | bool | `false` | `true`, `false` | Reads this source. |
| `plugins.openwrt.<instance>.host` | string | none, required | An address or host name, without a port | Where ubus is served. |
| `plugins.openwrt.<instance>.port` | int | `80`, or `443` with `ssl` | 1 to 65535 | uhttpd's port. |
| `plugins.openwrt.<instance>.user` | string | empty | An rpcd login | A login with the Jocasta ACL. |
| `plugins.openwrt.<instance>.password` | string | empty | Any | The login's password. |
| `plugins.openwrt.<instance>.ssl` | bool | `false` | `true`, `false` | Uses HTTPS. Needs `luci-ssl`. Without it, the password goes over the network as plain text, and Jocasta logs a warning. |
| `plugins.openwrt.<instance>.insecure` | bool | `false` | `true`, `false` | Skips certificate checks, for uhttpd's self-signed certificate. |
| `plugins.openwrt.<instance>.timeout` | duration | `10s` | A duration | The longest one read may take. |
| `plugins.openwrt.<instance>.topology_only` | bool | `false` | `true`, `false` | Reads only what is connected to this access point. The router lists its devices. See [Show what is plugged in where](<https://pushkar-anand.github.io/jocasta/0.15/plugins/topology/index.md>). |

### plugins.netflow

A [NetFlow](<https://pushkar-anand.github.io/jocasta/0.15/plugins/netflow/index.md>) listener for a router's flow exports.

| Key | Type | Default | Allowed values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `plugins.netflow.<instance>.enabled` | bool | `false` | `true`, `false` | Runs this listener. |
| `plugins.netflow.<instance>.listen` | string | `:2055` | A UDP address, such as `:2055` or `192.0.2.10:2055` | Where the listener binds. |
| `plugins.netflow.<instance>.exporters` | list | none, required | IP addresses | The routers that can send. Jocasta discards datagrams from all other addresses. |

### plugins.technitium

A [Technitium DNS Server](<https://pushkar-anand.github.io/jocasta/0.15/plugins/technitium/index.md>) node.

| Key | Type | Default | Allowed values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `plugins.technitium.<instance>.enabled` | bool | `false` | `true`, `false` | Reads this server's query log. |
| `plugins.technitium.<instance>.host` | string | none, required | An address or host name, without a port | The address of this node. Do not use a virtual address that the nodes share. It reaches only one node at a time. |
| `plugins.technitium.<instance>.port` | int | `5380`, or `53443` with `ssl` | 1 to 65535 | The web service's port. |
| `plugins.technitium.<instance>.token` | string | empty | An API token | A token for a user granted Logs: View. |
| `plugins.technitium.<instance>.ssl` | bool | `false` | `true`, `false` | Uses HTTPS. Without it, the token goes over the network as plain text, and Jocasta logs a warning. |
| `plugins.technitium.<instance>.insecure` | bool | `false` | `true`, `false` | Skips certificate checks, for a self-signed certificate. |
| `plugins.technitium.<instance>.log_app` | string | empty | An app name, as the Apps page lists it | The app whose log Jocasta reads. Necessary only if more than one installed app logs queries. |
| `plugins.technitium.<instance>.timeout` | duration | `10s` | A duration | The longest one read may take. |

### plugins.pihole

A [Pi-hole](<https://pushkar-anand.github.io/jocasta/0.15/plugins/pihole/index.md>) v6.

| Key | Type | Default | Allowed values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `plugins.pihole.<instance>.enabled` | bool | `false` | `true`, `false` | Reads this server's query log. |
| `plugins.pihole.<instance>.host` | string | none, required | An address or host name, without a port | Where Pi-hole's web server is. |
| `plugins.pihole.<instance>.port` | int | `80`, or `443` with `ssl` | 1 to 65535 | The web server's port. |
| `plugins.pihole.<instance>.password` | string | empty | An app password | Empty reads a Pi-hole with no password set. |
| `plugins.pihole.<instance>.ssl` | bool | `false` | `true`, `false` | Uses HTTPS. Without it, the password goes over the network as plain text, and Jocasta logs a warning. |
| `plugins.pihole.<instance>.insecure` | bool | `false` | `true`, `false` | Skips certificate checks, for Pi-hole's self-signed certificate. |
| `plugins.pihole.<instance>.timeout` | duration | `10s` | A duration | The longest one read may take. |

### plugins.adguard

An [AdGuard Home](<https://pushkar-anand.github.io/jocasta/0.15/plugins/adguard/index.md>).

| Key | Type | Default | Allowed values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `plugins.adguard.<instance>.enabled` | bool | `false` | `true`, `false` | Reads this server's query log. |
| `plugins.adguard.<instance>.host` | string | none, required | An address or host name, without a port | Where the web interface is. |
| `plugins.adguard.<instance>.port` | int | `80`, or `443` with `ssl` | 1 to 65535 | The web interface's port. |
| `plugins.adguard.<instance>.user` | string | empty | The web interface login | Empty reads a server with no login set. |
| `plugins.adguard.<instance>.password` | string | empty | Any | The login's password. |
| `plugins.adguard.<instance>.ssl` | bool | `false` | `true`, `false` | Uses HTTPS. Without it, the password goes over the network as plain text, and Jocasta logs a warning. |
| `plugins.adguard.<instance>.insecure` | bool | `false` | `true`, `false` | Skips certificate checks, for a self-signed certificate. |
| `plugins.adguard.<instance>.timeout` | duration | `10s` | A duration | The longest one read may take. |

## notify

Each destination is under `notify`, with a name that you choose as its key. It has exactly one service block: `ntfy`, `webhook` or `http`. To select the changes that a destination gets, use the Notifications page in the account menu. See [Notifications](<https://pushkar-anand.github.io/jocasta/0.15/notifications/index.md>).

| Key | Type | Default | Allowed values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `notify.<name>.enabled` | bool | `true` | `true`, `false` | Sends to this destination. A destination is on unless it says `false`. |
| `notify.<name>.timeout` | duration | `10s` | A duration | The longest one send may take. |

### ntfy

| Key | Type | Default | Allowed values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `notify.<name>.ntfy.url` | string | none, required | The topic's URL, as ntfy shows it | Where Jocasta publishes messages, such as `https://ntfy.example.com/jocasta`. |
| `notify.<name>.ntfy.token` | string | empty | An ntfy access token | For a server that requires one. |
| `notify.<name>.ntfy.priority` | int | `0` | `0` to `5` | ntfy's priority, from 1 (min) to 5 (max). `0` leaves it to the server. |

### webhook

| Key | Type | Default | Allowed values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `notify.<name>.webhook.url` | string | none, required | An HTTP or HTTPS URL | Where the signed JSON POST goes. |
| `notify.<name>.webhook.secret` | string | none, required | Any | Keys the signature on each request. See [Check a webhook's signature](<https://pushkar-anand.github.io/jocasta/0.15/notifications/webhook/index.md>). |

### http

| Key | Type | Default | Allowed values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `notify.<name>.http.url` | string | none, required | An HTTP or HTTPS URL | Where the request goes. It can contain the token of the service. Jocasta never logs or shows it. |
| `notify.<name>.http.headers` | map | empty | Header names and values | Sent with every request, such as `Authorization`. A `Content-Type` here replaces `application/json`. |
| `notify.<name>.http.body` | string | none, required | A Go template | The request body. See [Send to another service](<https://pushkar-anand.github.io/jocasta/0.15/notifications/other-services/index.md>) for recipes. |

# CLI

```
jocasta <command> [flags]

  serve              Start the web server and the sweep poller.  (default)
  scan <cidr>        Sweep a prefix once and print the result.
  ports [target]     Probe TCP ports on an address, a prefix, or the inventory.
  plugin run <name>  Read one configured source and print what it claims.
  version            Print build information.

  -c, --config       Path to the config file (default "jocasta.yaml")
      --log-level    debug | info | warn | error
      --log-format   text | json
```

To see the flags of a command, run it with `--help`.

## serve

```
jocasta serve                 # host and port from config
jocasta serve -p 9000         # override the port
```

Starts the HTTP server. It also starts these tasks:

- If `scan.devices.enabled` is set, a poller sweeps every network in `networks` at each `scan.devices.interval`.
- If `scan.ports.enabled` is set, a second poller port-scans every address that the inventory has on your networks, at each `scan.ports.interval`. It also port-scans each new device when a sweep or a router read finds it.
- At each `scan.devices.interval`, Jocasta reads each enabled `routeros` and `openwrt` instance for what is connected to it.
- Each enabled `netflow` instance starts a listener for the flow exports of its router.
- Each hour, a prune deletes records that are older than their `retention` window. It also deletes devices that you never edited and that no scan saw within `retention.devices`.

## scan

Runs one sweep and prints a table, or JSON with `--json`. With `--save`, it also records the sweep in the inventory. The source name comes from `--source`. If that is not set, it comes from `scan.source`, and then from the name of this host.

```
$ jocasta scan 192.0.2.0/24
IP           MAC                VENDOR   HOSTNAME              RTT     DETAILS
192.0.2.1    00:00:5e:00:53:01  -        gateway.example      1.2ms
192.0.2.10   00:00:5e:00:53:02  -        nas.example          0.8ms
192.0.2.20   00:00:5e:00:53:04  -        -                    3.1ms   self (eth0)

$ jocasta scan 192.0.2.0/24 --save --rate 500 --no-resolve-names
```

The sweep uses a raw ICMP socket if it can. If not, it uses an unprivileged datagram socket. So it runs without root. If a host has no reverse DNS name, the sweep asks for its name over mDNS, then NetBIOS, then DNS-SD, then SSDP. It stops when one of them gives a name. To turn each one off, use `--no-resolve-mdns`, `--no-resolve-netbios`, `--no-resolve-dnssd` or `--no-resolve-ssdp`. With `--json`, each host also lists the services that it advertises over DNS-SD.

## ports

Probes TCP ports with a plain `connect()`. So it needs no privileges and cannot change the target.

With no argument, it scans every current address that the inventory has on your networks. Your networks are those in `networks` and the segments that a router serves. It does not scan a neighbour outside them, such as the gateway of your ISP. It also scans each address on these TCP ports:

- the ports on which its device advertises a service
- the ports recorded as open on that device

To scan only one address or prefix, give it as the argument.

`--ports` takes a list such as `22,80,443,8000-8100`. By default, it scans a preset of about a hundred ports that homelabs often use. `--concurrency` sets the maximum number of open connections at one time (64 by default). `--save` records the results on the matching devices.

```
$ jocasta ports 192.0.2.10
ADDRESS      PORT   SERVICE
192.0.2.10   22     ssh
192.0.2.10   443    https

$ jocasta ports --save                      # every known address, recorded
$ jocasta ports 192.0.2.0/24 --ports 1-1024 --json
```

## plugin run

Reads one configured source without starting the server. Use it to test a credential or a firewall rule against the real router. It reads the instance even when the config disables it.

```
$ jocasta plugin run gateway
NETWORK           VLAN  NAME
192.0.2.0/24      -     Trusted
198.51.100.0/24   20    IoT

ADDRESS          MAC                VENDOR  HOSTNAME    STANDING     PRESENT
192.0.2.1        00:00:5e:00:53:01  -       gateway     DHCP_STATIC  true
198.51.100.10    00:00:5e:00:53:09  -       thermostat  DHCP_LEASE   true

$ jocasta plugin run gateway --json --save
```

After the devices, it prints the topology of the source:

- its ports, and the VLANs on each port
- the hardware addresses that it learned on each port
- its neighbours

A `topology_only` instance prints only the topology. `--save` records both.

# Development

# Development

## Make targets

```
make build          # build to bin/
make test           # go test ./...
make e2e            # browser tests a pull request must pass (needs Chrome)
make e2e-full       # browser tests on every screen and account
make smoke          # read the router, DNS and NetFlow sources in containers (needs Docker)
make lint           # golangci-lint (installs it to bin/ on first run)
make dev            # hot-reload server via air
make gen            # regenerate sqlc models
make new_migration name=<name>
make oui            # rebuild the embedded MAC-vendor table
make htmx           # refresh the vendored htmx
make docs           # build the docs site and check every link (needs uv)
make docs-serve     # preview the docs site at http://localhost:8000
```

## Browser tests

`internal/web/e2e` drives Chrome over the real server. It builds with the `e2e` tag, so `go test ./...` leaves it out. It needs Google Chrome or Chromium on `PATH`, or `E2E_CHROME` set to one of them.

The tests draw each page over four fabricated inventories: empty, a home network, a network with extreme data, and a network with no accounts. They also draw each dialog, menu and inline edit that the page opens. Each drawing is checked for these problems:

- sideways scrolling
- clipped or overlapping text
- small tap targets and small text
- WCAG 2.2 AA failures (axe-core)
- script errors and failed requests

`make e2e` draws every page as admin on a phone, a tablet and a laptop, in both themes. It takes about two minutes. CI does not run it. So run it before you open a pull request that changes the UI. `make e2e-full` adds every other screen and account. `scripts/release.sh` runs it before it tags a release.

A finding fails the run, unless `testdata/known.json` lists it under an open issue. A fix deletes its entries. `make e2e-full` also fails on an entry that no longer matches a finding.

The run also compares the first screen of every page on the home network with a stored picture in `testdata/golden/`. It does this on a phone, a tablet and a laptop in the light theme, and on the laptop in the dark theme. A picture fails when more than 64 of its pixels changed. One added or removed word changes more pixels than that. If you change the UI on purpose, store the new pictures and commit them with the change:

```
E2E_UPDATE=1 make e2e
```

To see what changed, set `E2E_ARTIFACTS` to a directory. The run writes each picture that differs there, next to a map of the changed pixels.

To look at a fixture in a browser:

```
E2E_SERVE=weird go test -tags e2e -run TestServe -timeout 0 ./internal/web/e2e/
```

To capture every page and read the findings, without a pass or fail:

```
E2E_AUDIT=$PWD/tmp/audit TMPDIR=$PWD/tmp go test -tags e2e -run TestAudit -timeout 0 ./internal/web/e2e/
```

To limit either run, set `E2E_FIXTURES`, `E2E_ROLES`, `E2E_VIEWPORTS`, `E2E_THEMES` or `E2E_PAGES` to a comma-separated list.

## Smoke tests

`make smoke` reads real OpenWrt, RouterOS, Pi-hole, AdGuard Home and Technitium servers and a real NetFlow exporter, each in a container. It checks what jocasta says about them. The plugin tests use canned replies. The smoke tests find a server that changed what it sends. They need Docker and Go. CI does not run them. So run them before you open a pull request that changes one of these plugins or its client under `pkg/`.

`scripts/smoke/smoke.sh up` starts the servers on their own network, `198.51.100.0/24`:

- OpenWrt has the setup that [the OpenWrt page](<https://pushkar-anand.github.io/jocasta/0.15/plugins/openwrt/index.md>) gives, with the ACL in `docs/openwrt/jocasta.json`. It also gets leases and static hosts.
- RouterOS CHR runs in QEMU, and `scripts/smoke/routeros.sh` boots it. Its `ether1` gets an address over DHCP, as a WAN port does. Its `ether2` is on the smoke network. It gets a read-only `jocasta` user, a bridge with its own address, a DHCP server with a static lease, and a static ARP entry. It also gets Traffic Flow that exports IPFIX, with the setup from [the RouterOS page](<https://pushkar-anand.github.io/jocasta/0.15/plugins/routeros/#export-traffic-flows>).
- Pi-hole, AdGuard Home and Technitium each block a name. AdGuard Home also rewrites one name. Technitium has the setup that [the Technitium page](<https://pushkar-anand.github.io/jocasta/0.15/plugins/technitium/index.md>) gives: a user that can view Logs, its API token, and the Query Logs (Sqlite) app. Pi-hole is the upstream of the other two, so no lookup leaves the network.
- pmacct runs in the network namespace of the OpenWrt container. It exports NetFlow v9 to this host, as the router would.
- The OpenWrt container sends lookups to each resolver.

Each server publishes its web interface on `127.0.0.1`, and jocasta reads it there.

`scripts/smoke/smoke.sh check` runs `jocasta plugin run` against each server and checks the rows that it prints. It also runs these tests:

- `TestNetFlowLive` in `internal/plugin`, two times. The first time, the OpenWrt container makes a lookup. The second time, this host makes a request to the router. The script checks the flows that each run decodes.
- The live tests in `pkg/openwrt`, `pkg/routeros` and `internal/plugin`.

The script writes its config to `$TMPDIR/jocasta-smoke/jocasta.yaml`. So you can point `jocasta serve` at the same servers. `make smoke-down` removes the servers.

Some services need more than Docker. To leave a service out, add it to `SMOKE_SKIP`, such as `SMOKE_SKIP="technitium netflow" make smoke`:

- `routeros`: RouterOS runs under QEMU. If the host has no KVM, QEMU emulates the CPU. In both cases, it boots in less than a minute. Its container joins a second network, which needs Docker 28 or later.
- `technitium`: the server downloads the Query Logs app from the app store of Technitium. So its container needs internet access.
- `netflow`: the exporter sends to the gateway address of the network. Only Docker on Linux puts this address on the host.

To change a setting, set the matching variable:

- `SMOKE_REGISTRY` pulls the images from a mirror, such as `mirror.gcr.io`. Use it when Docker Hub limits your pulls.
- `SMOKE_PIHOLE_IMAGE`, `SMOKE_ADGUARD_IMAGE`, `SMOKE_OPENWRT_IMAGE`, `SMOKE_ROUTEROS_IMAGE`, `SMOKE_TECHNITIUM_IMAGE` and `SMOKE_PMACCT_IMAGE` test a different release. MikroTik publishes no image. The RouterOS image is `evilfreelancer/docker-routeros`, which contains the CHR disk and QEMU.
- `SMOKE_PIHOLE_PORT`, `SMOKE_ADGUARD_PORT`, `SMOKE_ADGUARD_SETUP_PORT`, `SMOKE_OPENWRT_PORT`, `SMOKE_TECHNITIUM_PORT` and `SMOKE_ROUTEROS_PORT` change the published ports, 18081 to 18086 by default. `SMOKE_FLOW_PORT` and `SMOKE_ROUTEROS_FLOW_PORT` change the ports for the NetFlow and IPFIX exports, 2055 and 2056 by default.

netifd cannot create the `br-lan` bridge in a container. So the `lan` of the OpenWrt container is on `eth0`. Its bridge table and VLANs are empty. The unit tests cover the reads of these tables.

## Docs

[Zensical](<https://zensical.org>) publishes the pages in `docs/` to GitHub Pages. There is one version for each minor release and one for `main`. The `Docs` workflow builds every pull request that changes the docs with `make docs`. This build fails on a broken link or anchor. A merge to `main` publishes the `dev` version. A `v*` tag publishes its minor version as `latest`. The Zensical fork of [mike](<https://github.com/squidfunk/mike>) pushes both to the `gh-pages` branch.

When you change the docs:

- Add a new page to `nav` in `mkdocs.yml`, and to the `llmstxt` sections there. If you do not, the site leaves it out of the sidebar and `llms.txt`.
- A new plugin gets a page under `docs/plugins/` and a line in the table on the plugins overview. A DNS resolver also gets a column on [Record what devices look up](<https://pushkar-anand.github.io/jocasta/0.15/plugins/dns/index.md>).
- A new setting gets a row in the [configuration reference](<https://pushkar-anand.github.io/jocasta/0.15/reference/configuration/index.md>). `TestReferenceDocumentsEveryKey` fails until the setting has a row. It also fails on a row for a setting that no longer exists.
- Keep `docs/setup.md` and `docs/mcp.md`. Earlier releases link to their sections on GitHub. Each section there points to the new location.

## Release

After CI passes on `main`, run the command below. It runs `make e2e-full` first, so Chrome must be installed.

```
./scripts/release.sh v0.10.0
```

The script needs a clean working tree and a local `main` that matches `origin/main`. It checks that the tag is not used. Then it creates an annotated tag and pushes it, which starts the release workflow. It does not wait for the build.

git-cliff writes the GitHub release and the changelog page from the commit messages, as `cliff.toml` sets. To give a minor release highlights, merge `docs/releases/<major.minor>.md` before you tag its `.0`.

## Layout

- `cmd/jocasta`: CLI entry point.
- `internal/scanner`: the ICMP sweep, and the reverse DNS, mDNS, NetBIOS, DNS-SD and SSDP lookups that name the hosts that answer.
- `internal/plugin`: sources other than the sweep (RouterOS, OpenWrt, NetFlow, Technitium, Pi-hole, AdGuard Home).
- `internal/inventory`: the store. It covers identity resolution, address handling, device classification and the change log.
- `internal/classify`: the rules that guess the type of a device from its vendor, name and open ports.
- `internal/notify`: sends the changes of each finished scan to ntfy, a webhook or a templated HTTP request.
- `internal/web`, `internal/api`: the HTML UI and the JSON API.
- `internal/db`: connection, migrations, generated queries.

SQLC generates the queries from `internal/db/queries/`. The schema is in `internal/db/migrations/`.

## Add a notification service

Most services accept an HTTP request. The `http` provider reaches them with a body template and no new code. For such a service, add a recipe to [Send to another service](<https://pushkar-anand.github.io/jocasta/0.15/notifications/other-services/index.md>). `TestRecipesInTheDocsRender` renders every recipe on that page. So a broken recipe fails the tests.

A service gets its own provider only when the `http` provider cannot reach it. For example, the service needs more than one request, a protocol other than HTTP, or a signature that a template cannot make. Each provider is in its own file in `internal/notify`, as `ntfy.go` and `webhook.go` are:

1. Add a struct with `koanf` tags for its settings. Give it `Validate`, `Host` and `Send`. `Send` must not put a credential in its error. For a service that accepts an HTTP request, use `post`.
2. Add a field for it to `notify.Config`, and a line to `Config.provider`.
3. Add an example to `jocasta.example.yaml`. Add a row for each setting to the [configuration reference](<https://pushkar-anand.github.io/jocasta/0.15/reference/configuration/index.md>).

The notifier, the settings page, the store and `cmd` need no change.

## Add a name source

Each name has a standing, `dbtype.HostnameSource`, which tells how Jocasta learned it. If sources give different names, Jocasta shows the name with the higher standing.

1. Add a constant for it in `internal/db/dbtype/enum.go`, and add it to `hostnameSources`.
2. Give it a place in `HostnameSource.Rank`. Give the reason in the comment there. A name that resolves ranks above a name that a device only claims.
3. Write its device page text in `standing`, in `internal/web/funcs.go`.
4. List it in [Name devices](<https://pushkar-anand.github.io/jocasta/0.15/naming/index.md>).

If a sweep asks devices for their names, do two more steps:

1. Add its lookup in its own file in `internal/scanner`. Ask it in `enrich`, in rank order. A query that goes to each host is a `nameProtocol`, as in `mdns.go` and `netbios.go`. Any other lookup is a `nameLookup`, as `askSSDP` in `ssdp.go` is. Or it names hosts itself, as `browseServices` does with `dnssd.go`.
2. Add it to `HostnameSource.Swept`. Then a lookup with a lower rank never replaces its name on the claim of the sweep.

The column has no CHECK, so a new standing needs no migration.

## Screenshots

The images in [`docs/ui.md`](<https://pushkar-anand.github.io/jocasta/0.15/ui/index.md>) come from a database of fabricated devices, never real network data: addresses from RFC 5737, hardware addresses from RFC 7042, and invented names. The internet peers are well-known public services, so Jocasta can find their organisations and countries.
